prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Purpose: original buildable environment concept art for a premium survival game set in an abandoned, drowned subtropical coastal city several generations after people left. Invent solely from this written description. No photographs, no other game's imagery, no existing franchise designs.
Medium: polished digital PAINTING in stylized realism, high-end game art, confident designed forms, rich tactile materials, believable warm late-afternoon sunlight and cool sky fill in shadows. Handsome, restrained, specific. Not photoreal photography, not cartoon, not loose sketch.
Palm construction: every crown consists of distinct pinnate feather fronds with a visible midrib, many slim leaflets on both sides, a rising arch and drooping tip. Open wedges of sky between fronds; clear radial crown star. Never fan palms, banana leaves, fern blobs or fuzzy green balls. Individual trees vary in age, height, lean, crown fullness, missing fronds and minor scars. All crowns grow radially in 3D and work from every azimuth.
Royal: nearly straight smooth pale grey column, subtle swell below mid-height, taper toward a glossy bright green 1.5–2 m crownshaft, 3–4 m arching fronds, compact elevated crown; mature height 14–20 m, trunk about 0.5 m wide with 0.6 m swell. Coconut: slender grey-brown ringed trunk 9–14 m along its curve, 0.3–0.4 m wide, leaning outward then rising, occasional kink/S curve, broad loose 8–10 m crown of 4–5 m drooping fronds, coconuts and old flower stalks just under crown, 0–3 hanging dead brown fronds. Bases flare gently into very tight low mats of thin roots immediately around the trunk, never sprawling roots, buttresses or root stilts.
Output: one finished PNG, landscape canvas, maximum native resolution available; aim for 3840 x 2160. No watermark or decorative border.
Asset: palm_parts.png. An exceptionally clear, spacious professionally painted botanical asset construction board on a plain warm grey/off-white background. Landscape canvas at the largest native resolution available. Eleven individually separated specimen studies, in three broad horizontal rows. Each is a finished detailed material/construction painting, not a sketch or a photograph. Clean small dark sans-serif labels exactly as specified below, one label per study; no paragraph text. Thin leader lines only where necessary. Arrange so nothing collides, no decorative frame.
Top row, four equally spaced closeups:
1. "ROYAL — FOOT": pale smooth 0.55 m trunk meeting cracked pavement, slight low basal flare, dense narrow mat of fine tangled 2–10 mm roots disappearing into pavement cracks immediately at base. No buttress or broad root spread.
2. "ROYAL — CROWNSHAFT": large 1.8 m glossy lime/emerald green smooth cylinder between grey trunk and radial crown, visibly overlapping smooth leaf sheaths; show EXACT attachment where separate live frond petioles peel from TOP of shaft around all azimuths, lower frond arches drooping past it. Not a bunch of leaves attached all down cylinder.
3. "COCONUT — FOOT": ringed grey-brown trunk flaring from 0.35 m to a 0.75 m basal swelling; low thin root mat gripping sand beside broken concrete, flush with ground.
4. "COCONUT — CROWN / BELOW": look straight upward at open star-shaped radial arrangement of frond bases, six to ten clearly separated midribs projecting in all directions with near foreshortened leaflets; clustered green, yellow and brown coconuts tucked among thick petiole bases, branching ochre old flower stalks underneath; no green crownshaft.
Middle row, four studies on SAME scale within each species pair:
5. "ROYAL FROND — TOP / 3.6 m": isolated single long narrow pinnate frond laid flat, viewed exactly from above, entire 3.6 m rachis with narrow feather leaflets on BOTH sides tapering at both ends, long bare proximal petiole.
6. "ROYAL FROND — SIDE": the same isolated frond in true side elevation, full petiole rising then bowing over into a long drooping tip, leaflets hanging below its midrib, no trunk.
7. "COCONUT FROND — TOP / 4.6 m": isolated single 4.6 m elongated pinnate frond laid flat from above, heavier central rachis, long regularly alternating straplike leaflets on BOTH sides and distinctly tapering tip, basal bare petiole.
8. "COCONUT FROND — SIDE": same frond in true side elevation with a broad high arch then deep downward distal sweep, leaflets drooping below, entire leaf visible.
Bottom row, three large studies:
9. "DEAD FROND": entire curled skeletal cinnamon/umber brown dead palm frond, intact rigid arched midrib and broken folded hanging straw leaflets, dry torn fibrous base.
10. "ROYAL — TRUNK SURFACE": arm's-length material closeup of a gently round smooth pale grey column, soft fine powdery patina, sparse subtle nearly horizontal pale ring scars and one shallow old impact scar, warm sun side and cool shade.
11. "COCONUT — TRUNK SURFACE": arm's-length material closeup of a narrower curved grey-brown column with compressed irregular transverse rings, fine longitudinal fibres, worn warm ridges and dark shallow recesses, no deeply furrowed oak bark.
Keep relative scale sensible within each drawing; these are enlarged detail views so do not add a full-size human to the parts. Small 10 cm scale bars at feet and surface studies only if space permits. Prioritize unambiguous anatomy and clear frond top-vs-side geometry.
